task.problem:
Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial; X is connected and compact. All potentials are genuine canonical psh-plus-smooth representatives. Let n>=2. Assume X has a smooth positive balanced Hermitian form beta with d(beta^(n-1))=0 and a smooth positive pluriclosed Hermitian form omega with dd^c omega=0. They may be different metrics. The associated conjecture is that X is Kahler, i.e. admits a smooth d-closed positive real (1,1)-form. The original programme asks to use this coexistence to construct closed positive data (a closed Kahler current would suffice), or to control a geometric flow changing torsion; identify the estimate beyond finite balanced trace that prevents metric degeneration, and determine whether Gauduchon determinant estimates can provide it. The flow variant also assumes c1(X)=0 in real cohomology and asks for long-time existence and convergence of pluriclosed flow to a Kahler metric. If a flow is used, specify its evolution, normalization, admissible initial data and precise convergence. The standard pluriclosed evolution uses minus the (1,1) part of the Bismut Ricci form; time-scale conventions must be specified. A single metric both balanced and pluriclosed is already Kahler. A pluriclosed manifold in Fujiki class is known Kahler. Finite conserved balanced trace in invariant examples is not pointwise ellipticity and does not preclude degeneration. Scalar potential perturbations preserve d(omega+dd^c u)=d omega, so prescribing a volume cannot itself remove torsion. Let h be a smooth Hermitian metric and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Let G_h consist of all positive (n-1,n-1)-currents T with dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. Write sigma_T=h wedge T; in an h-unitary frame let P_T be the positive Hermitian matrix density characterized by beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_T)d sigma_T, tr(P_T)=n, for B the h-relative matrix of any smooth (1,1)-form beta. The determinant measure Gamma_0(T)=(dV/h^n)^(1/n)det(P_T)^(1/n)sigma_T is absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Define k_T=d Gamma_0(T)/dV. For smooth strictly positive T=gamma^(n-1), k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n). The family G_h includes singular and degenerate currents, and the endpoint is over all currents, not only smooth exact maximizers. Define v_minus(h) as the infimum of the total bounded-potential Monge-Ampere masses over all bounded genuine h-psh potentials. No candidate geometric condition, flow estimate or proof is supplied.

Conventions: X is connected compact complex, n>=2, ddc=i partial
barpartial/(2pi), ordinary wedges, fixed positive smooth probability dV.
Bounded potentials are genuine canonical psh-plus-smooth representatives.
G_h consists of ALL positive (n-1,n-1) currents T with ddc T=0 and
integral h wedge T=1. Include all singular and degenerate coefficients.
For any auxiliary positive Hermitian h, sigma_h=h wedge T and its
trace-normalized relative density matrix P_h has trace n and satisfies
xi wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_h)sigma_h. Define
Gamma_(0,h)(T)=(dV/h^n)^(1/n)det(P_h)^(1/n)sigma_h.

A. For every positive current T, even without ddc-closedness, this is
a finite intrinsic Radon measure independent of auxiliary h. Verify
all coordinate changes and choices of coefficient-dominating measure,
including mutually singular coefficient measures and rank deficiency.

B. Let beta be smooth positive Hermitian, possibly genuinely nonclosed,
with ddc(beta^j)=0 for EVERY j=1,...,n-1. Put V=integral beta^n.
For EVERY bounded canonical beta-psh w, the actual bounded Hermitian
MA product satisfies integral(beta+ddc w)^n=V. Both bounded mass
extrema therefore equal V. The signed closed powers E^b of E=ddc w
are globally well-defined by local bounded products with smooth psh
corrections and satisfy E^b=ddc[w E^(b-1)]. Verify this recursion,
overlap independence and pairing with nonclosed smooth beta^a; do not
assume beta is the curvature of a local closed potential.
For smooth w, A=beta+ddc w has ddc(A^j)=0 for j<=n-1 and
integral beta wedge A^(n-1)=V. No d-closedness of beta is assumed.

C. Under exactly B's differential hypotheses, for every smooth
global real u with h=beta+ddc u>0 the ACTUAL current sets G_h=G_beta
and the ENTIRE intrinsic determinant-measure families agree.
For EVERY T in that family Gamma0(T)=k_T dV with k_T>=0 and
norm_(L^(n/(n-1)))k_T<=V^(-1/n). Prove absolute continuity instead
of importing it as an assumption. For EVERY real/complex p in Ln(dV),
sup_(ALL T in G_h) integral |p|Gamma0(T)=V^(-1/n)norm_Ln p.
Retain arbitrary positive smooth probability dV and all currents.
For smooth r>0, M=integral r^n dV, there is a smooth positive
A=beta+ddc v with A^n=(V r^n/M)dV. The source normalization must be
justified for this nonclosed background. T_r=A^(n-1)/V is an ACTUAL
positive ddc-closed normalized current, with
k_(T_r)=V^(-1/n)r^(n-1)/norm_Ln(r)^(n-1), attaining the endpoint.

D. On X=(C/(Z+iZ))^n let zj=xj+i yj, beta_j=(i/2)dzj wedge
dbar zj, beta=sum beta_j, V=n!, dV=beta^n/V. For 0<epsilon<=1 put
u_epsilon=(1-epsilon)cos(4pi x1)/(4pi),
a_epsilon=1-(1-epsilon)cos(4pi x1),
omega_epsilon=beta+ddc u_epsilon=a_epsilon beta1+sum_(j>=2)beta_j.
Verify global periodicity, positivity and closedness, minimum relative
eigenvalue epsilon, omega_epsilon<=2beta, uniform fixed-order smooth
norms of coefficients and potentials, and a smooth semipositive limit.
The entire current/measure families and exact C endpoint are identical,
and BOTH bounded-potential mass extrema equal V. X has trivial
canonical bundle and ordinary real c1=0; all omega_epsilon are already
Kahler, balanced and pluriclosed.

E. On the SAME torus fix 0<tau<1/2, s=sin(2pi x1),
xi=(i/2)(dz1 wedge dbar z2+dz2 wedge dbar z1)
   =dx1 wedge dy2+dx2 wedge dy1,
h_tau=beta+tau s xi,
Omega_epsilon=h_tau+ddc u_epsilon
 =a_epsilon beta1+sum_(j>=2)beta_j+tau s xi, 0<epsilon<=1/2.
These are positive GENUINELY NONCLOSED pluriclosed metrics,
dOmega_epsilon=dh_tau=2pi tau cos(2pi x1)dx1 wedge dx2 wedge dy1,
not identically zero. Verify ddc(h_tau^j)=ddc(Omega_epsilon^j)=0
for every j<=n-1, including all higher dimensions and the actual
two-factor product expansion. V_tau=integral h_tau^n=n!(1-tau^2/2).
Their least beta-relative eigenvalue is exactly epsilon; they obey
epsilon beta<=Omega_epsilon<=3beta, uniform fixed-order smooth
coefficient and potential bounds, and a smooth rank-deficient limit.
Their ACTUAL full current and measure sets agree with G_h_tau and
their endpoint equals V_tau^(-1/n)norm_Ln(p) for EVERY p and ALL
currents with any fixed positive smooth probability dV.
BOTH bounded-potential mass extrema equal V_tau and the balanced
trace integral Omega_epsilon wedge beta^(n-1)=n! is fixed.
The fixed beta is balanced, distinct from these pluriclosed metrics;
X has c1=0 and is already Kahler. No non-Kahler manifold is asserted.

F. Additional concentration on the same torus in EVERY n>=2.
For 0<epsilon<1 let r=1-epsilon,
P_r(x)=(1-r^2)/(1-2r cos(2pi x)+r^2),
f_epsilon=epsilon+(1-epsilon)P_r(x1),
w_epsilon=-(2(1-epsilon)/pi)sum_(m>=1)r^m cos(2pi m x1)/m^2,
A_epsilon=beta+ddc w_epsilon=f_epsilon beta1+sum_(j>=2)beta_j,
T_epsilon=A_epsilon^(n-1)/V in G_beta.
Their densities satisfy k_(T_epsilon)=V^(-1/n)f_epsilon^((n-1)/n),
integral k_(T_epsilon)^(n/(n-1))dV=V^(-1/(n-1)), attaining the
sharp bound over ALL currents. For the VARYING unit Ln root
p_epsilon=f_epsilon^(1/n), T_epsilon is an actual dual maximizer.
No single common fixed density and no uniform coefficient bounds
are asserted for this concentrating family.
Potentials obey |w_epsilon|<=pi/3 and converge uniformly to the
continuous canonical beta-psh w0=-(2/pi)sum cos(2pi m x1)/m^2.
The actual bounded BT currents converge weakly to
T0=(beta+ddc w0)^(n-1)/V in G_beta, while Gamma0(T0)=0.
The determinant POWER densities are not uniformly integrable and
their integrals are not continuous under these weak current limits.
The Gamma0 measures themselves converge to zero in total mass.
Every w_epsilon including w0 nevertheless has genuine bounded
potential MA mass V. Distinguish the three different measures.

G. These fixed entire determinant data alone, even with constant
positive bounded mass extrema, c1=0 and uniform smooth coefficient
and potential bounds, do not force a positive pointwise lower metric
bound, including the genuinely nonclosed pluriclosed family E with
fixed nonzero exterior derivative and a separate balanced metric.
No family is a pluriclosed-flow trajectory; epsilon is not flow time.
Additional density, torsion-norm or initial pointwise flow controls
are not excluded. Neither unrestricted original P13 conjecture nor
literature priority is certified. The two-factor torsion mechanism
itself is not claimed new.

task.completionCriteria: Prove closed positive data or precise geometric-flow control from the balanced/pluriclosed coexistence, addressing the estimate needed beyond finite balanced trace and the role or limitation of full Gauduchon determinant bounds. A general Kahlerness or long-time flow claim must retain every original hypothesis and prove every conclusion. A genuinely new fully specified sufficient-condition theorem may be recorded as restricted, but cannot close the unrestricted coexistence or flow conjectures. A restatement of the same-metric case, conserved total trace or scalar prescribed-volume equation is insufficient. Verify indispensable external premises at primary sources and independently reconstruct every theorem. Independently reconstruct or reject every restricted A--G. An exact determinant-profile limitation is not a construction of closed positive data or a geometric-flow trajectory. Judge original completion separately, keeping the unrestricted conjectures open unless their full conclusions have actually been proved.
